requirements.text: their premium support contract ... finance wants the amount rebalanced to around 99.108 grand dollar
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM contract WHERE contract_id = 101 AND contract_price = 99108
assumptions: 'Russell, Johnson and Clark' is account 40; 'support contract' read as contract_type = support, contract 101 (seed price 2537, status draft), the account's only support contract and the one the benchmark tests; its warranty contract 100 carries the premium entitlement and is the other reading
'99.108 grand dollar' is 99108 dollars; the policy's rounding rule applies only if decimals remain, and none do; 'around' taken as the exact figure the benchmark tests
status (draft), type and dates not touched: the request narrows 'contract details' to the amount

requirements.text: be sure the contact is associated with the correct location Smith Llc Hq - London
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user WHERE user_id = 55 AND location_id = 903
assumptions: the primary contact of account 40 is contact 89 (is_primary 1), portal user 55 Bethany Barnes (seed location 55 'User 55 - Sydney'); contact has no location column, so the association is user.location_id
'Smith Llc Hq - London' resolved by name to location 903 (active) although it is another account's site; the account's own 'Russell, Johnson And Clark Hq - London' (881) is not what the request names

disagreement: structure: B carries the benchmark check in one change requirement with both the location and the phone, A splits it into this change and a stay on the phone; kept A's split because the phone is a replacement the request forbids when its condition is false, which is a stay, while the location is a change; both carry the same source and the two sqls together test what B's one did

requirements.text: only if that's the case [the profile might still be carrying that old India branch number], go ahead and replace it with their new JPN number
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user WHERE user_id = 55 AND phone = '+12125516299'
assumptions: user 55's phone +12125516299 is not an India (+91) number, so the condition for the replacement is not met and the phone must stay at its seed value; the benchmark check tests the same

requirements.text: check their primary contact ... old India branch number, and only if that's the case ... replace it
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user WHERE user_id IN (681, 726) AND phone LIKE '+91%'
assumptions: boundary of 'primary contact': the account's two non-primary contacts (contacts 90 and 91, users 681 and 726) do carry +91 numbers, which a reading that drops 'primary' would replace

disagreement: cells: A {phone: LIKE '+91%'} with the predicate repeated in the selector, B {} with it in the selector only; chose selector user_id IN (681, 726) with the LIKE predicate as the cell, so the rows are picked by key and the tested column is in cells; the sql is the same in both passes

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM contract WHERE contract_id = 100 AND contract_price = 2142
assumptions: boundary of the contract selector: contract 100 (warranty, active) is the one the premium entitlement 344 points at, the near-match for 'premium support contract'; a reading through the entitlement would reprice it instead

notes: Merged from two passes that agree on both benchmark checks (kept), the contract (101 to 99108), the primary contact (user 55), the location (903), the phone that stays (+12125516299, the conditional does not fire) and the two boundary stays (the non-primary contacts' +91 numbers and contract 100's price). disagreement: the user check's structure: B carries it in one change requirement with both cells, A splits it into the location change and a stay on the phone; kept A's split (logged in the location requirement). disagreement: cells of the +91 stay: A repeats the predicate as the cell, B leaves cells empty; chose selector by user id with the phone predicate as the cell (logged in the requirement). Both passes name the same least-sure reading, which is not a disagreement: 'their premium support contract' is the support-type contract 101 (as the benchmark tests), not the warranty contract 100 that carries the premium entitlement; the stay on 100 guards the other reading. The acting user Jose Roberson (32) is an admin but active = 0 on the seed; this policy says to assume the admin role by default and says nothing about inactive actors, so this is recorded, not treated as blocking. Contract 101 is in status 'draft', a value the schema allows but the policy's enumeration omits; the request asks for no status change, so none is required.
